tut.basics.activate.s1.text:
Activating a mod performs these steps automatically:
  • 1. BMM reads the mapping plan for the mod
  • 2. It computes a SHA-256 fingerprint for every file it will overwrite
  • 3. Original files are saved to your Backup Folder
  • 4. Mod files are physically copied to the game directory
Deactivating is the exact reverse — originals are restored from backup.
💡

Your game files are always recoverable — BMM keeps 3 independent backup layers even if one fails.
tut.basics.activate.s1.title: How Activation Works
tut.basics.activate.s2.action: Flip the toggle switch on any mod card to ON.
tut.basics.activate.s2.text: Use the toggle switch on the left of any mod card in the Library. BMM copies the mod's files and shows a progress bar for large mods. The card turns green and shows an activation order number (#1, #2…) when done.
tut.basics.activate.s2.title: Enable a Mod
tut.basics.activate.s3.action: Flip the same mod's toggle switch back to OFF.
tut.basics.activate.s3.text: Toggle the switch back Off. BMM looks up the backup it saved during activation and restores every original file. The order number disappears and the card returns to inactive state.
tut.basics.activate.s3.title: Disable a Mod
tut.basics.activate.s4.text: When two active mods touch the same game file, the one with the higher activation order number wins (activated later = higher priority). You can see each mod's order number on its card, and reorder by dragging from the detail panel.
tut.basics.activate.s4.title: Activation Order
tut.basics.activate.title: Activating Mods
tut.basics.conflicts.s1.text: Each mod card shows INTRA and/or INTER conflict badges. INTRA = conflicting files inside the same mod's profile. INTER = the same game file is touched by two different mods across profiles. Click any badge to open the Global Conflict View with full details, file counts, and activation order.
tut.basics.conflicts.s1.title: Conflict Detection
tut.basics.conflicts.s2.text: In Settings → Storage, the I/O Limiter caps disk throughput during activation to prevent system lag on slow drives or NAS setups. Run the built-in Benchmark first to find the best limit for your hardware.
tut.basics.conflicts.s2.title: Storage Manager (I/O Limiter)
tut.basics.conflicts.title: Conflicts & Storage
tut.basics.integrity.s1.text:
Every file BMM tracks gets a SHA-256 hash — a 64-character fingerprint computed from the file's exact bytes. Change a single byte and the hash changes completely.

BMM records these fingerprints when a mod is added, giving it a trustworthy "before" snapshot. Later it recomputes the hashes and compares, so it knows with certainty whether a file is still the one you installed.
💡

Hashes catch silent corruption — a half-finished download, a game patch that overwrote a mod file, or disk errors — none of which change the file name or size.
tut.basics.integrity.s1.title: What is SHA/Hash Verification?
tut.basics.integrity.s2.action: Click Verify in the Library toolbar to run an integrity check.
tut.basics.integrity.s2.text:
If a mod misbehaves after a game update, click Verify in the Library toolbar. BMM recomputes every tracked file's hash and compares it to the stored fingerprint, flagging each file as:
  • OK — matches the stored hash ✓
  • Modified — contents changed since install
  • Missing — the file was deleted or moved
tut.basics.integrity.s2.title: Run an Integrity Check
tut.basics.integrity.title: Integrity & Hashes
tut.basics.map.s1.text:
The Mapper is where you tell BMM where inside your game folder each mod's files should be placed. Without a correct mapping, activating a mod would drop files in the wrong place — or nowhere at all.

The Mapper shows two trees side by side: your mod's file tree on the left, and your game's directory on the right. Your job is to make the left tree match the right one.
tut.basics.map.s1.title: What is the Mapper?
tut.basics.map.s2.text:
First, pick a Profile from the top-left dropdown. This tells BMM which game directory to load on the right panel.

Once selected, the right panel fills with your game's folder structure — for example:
Game RootC:/Games/MyGame/
💡

If the game tree looks empty, make sure the Profile's Game Path is correctly set in the Profiles page.
tut.basics.map.s2.title: Step 1 — Select a Profile
tut.basics.map.s3.text:
The game directory usually has a dedicated Mods folder where mod files must be placed. Common names are:
  • Mods/
  • Data/
  • Content/
Browse the right-panel tree and find it. That folder is your target destination — your mod's files must land inside it (or a subfolder of it) to work correctly.
tut.basics.map.s3.title: Step 2 — Find the Mods Folder
tut.basics.map.s4.text:
Now pick a Mod from the top-right dropdown. Its internal file tree appears on the left panel.

Read the left tree carefully. Ask yourself: does this structure match what the game expects?
  • Is there a top-level folder that matches Mods/?
  • Or do the files start at root level (bad — they would install to the game root)?
  • Is there an extra wrapper folder that adds a wrong level of nesting?
tut.basics.map.s4.title: Step 3 — Read the Mod Tree
tut.basics.map.s5.text:
A common problem: a mod archive contains MyMod/files/texture.dds but the game expects files directly in Mods/texture.dds.

To remap, it's a two-click action:
  • ① Select a file or folder in the mod tree on the left (hold Ctrl to select several at once).
  • ② Double-click the destination folder in the game tree on the right.
BMM re-roots the selected items into that folder in one move — no manual renaming.
⚠️

Nothing is changed on disk yet. The Mapper only builds a mapping plan — changes apply only when you click APPLY STRUCTURE.
tut.basics.map.s5.title: Step 4 — Fix the Structure
tut.basics.map.s6.text:
The Destination Folder field at the bottom of the left panel shows the final install path for the mod. This is the folder that will be written inside your game directory on activation.

Example — if your game expects mods in Mods/ and your mod has a root folder SuperMod/, set the destination to:
DestinationMods/SuperMod/
Set it using the two-click mapping from Step 4 (select on the left, double-click the target folder on the right), or type the path directly in the field.
tut.basics.map.s6.title: Step 5 — Set the Destination
tut.basics.map.s7.action: Click the Preview button to open the full mapping diagnostic.
tut.basics.map.s7.text:
Click Preview to open the full mapping diagnostic. BMM maps every mod file to its game path and color-codes the result:
  • Green — file maps to a valid game path ✓
  • Yellow — file is at root level (will not install correctly)
  • Red — no matching folder found in the game tree ✗
Fix any yellow or red entries by adjusting the destination, then click APPLY STRUCTURE to save the plan.
tut.basics.map.s7.title: Step 6 — Preview & Apply
tut.basics.map.title: Mapping (File Structure)
tut.basics.meta.desc: Learn what BMM can do: isolated profiles per game, automatic mod scanning, safe activation with full backup, file integrity verification, conflict detection, and shared folders for multi-profile setups.
tut.basics.meta.title: BMM Modding Basics
tut.basics.modpacks.s1.text: A Modpack is a curated group of mods that can be toggled on or off together with a single click. Perfect for managing 'load orders' or themed sets of mods for different scenarios.
tut.basics.modpacks.s1.title: What is a Modpack?
tut.basics.modpacks.s2.action: Go to Modpacks, click "Create Modpack", add a few mods with "Add Mods", then click "Save Modpack".
tut.basics.modpacks.s2.text:
Open the Modpacks page and click Create Modpack. In the editor:
  • Give the pack a name (and an optional description).
  • Click Add Mods to pick mods from your library — each one is listed with a Remove button if you change your mind.
  • Click Save Modpack to keep it, or Cancel to discard.
Later, enabling a modpack turns on all of its mods at once; disabling it turns them all off.
tut.basics.modpacks.s2.title: Create a Modpack
tut.basics.modpacks.title: Creating a Modpack
tut.basics.profiles.s1.text: A Profile is a workspace for a specific game configuration. Each one has its own game path, mods folder, and backup directory. Think of it as a dedicated slot for each game you mod.
tut.basics.profiles.s1.title: What are Profiles?
tut.basics.profiles.s2.action: Open Profiles, click "Create a profile", fill the four fields explained above, then click Create.
tut.basics.profiles.s2.text:
Open the Profiles page and click Create a profile. Before you create it, here is what each field does:
  • Name — a label for this workspace (e.g. "Skyrim — Heavy").
  • Game path — the game's root folder; this is where active mods get installed.
  • Mods folder — where BMM keeps this profile's mod library (scanned, not yet installed).
  • Backup folder — where original game files are safely copied before a mod overwrites them, so activation is always reversible.
Once the four fields are filled, click Create — BMM sets up an isolated workspace just for this game.
tut.basics.profiles.s2.title: Create your first Profile
tut.basics.profiles.s3.text:
Three folders matter for every profile:
  • Game Path — the root folder where the game is installed (contains the game .exe)
  • Mods Folder — where your mod subfolders live; BMM scans this to discover mods
  • Backup Folder — where BMM saves original game files before overwriting them
⚠️

Never share a Mods Folder between two profiles — activating a mod for the wrong game could corrupt its installation.
tut.basics.profiles.s3.title: The Three Paths
tut.basics.profiles.s4.text: Each profile can have a custom background and a color accent. Click the Edit icon (pencil) on any profile card to personalize it. BMM includes a built-in cropping tool for background images.
tut.basics.profiles.s4.title: Custom Background & Colors
tut.basics.profiles.title: Profile Management
tut.basics.scan.s0.text: Go to Profiles and make sure at least one profile is active (highlighted with a colored border). The active profile defines where BMM looks for mods and where it installs them. Without an active profile, Library and Mapper won't work.
tut.basics.scan.s0.title: Check Your Active Profile
tut.basics.scan.s1.text: A scan reads your profile's Mods Folder and registers every subfolder it finds as a mod entry. It is completely non-destructive — no file is moved, copied, or modified. It's just discovery.
tut.basics.scan.s1.title: What is a Mod Scan?
tut.basics.scan.s2.action: Click the Scan button in the Library toolbar — mods will appear in the list.
tut.basics.scan.s2.text: Switch to the Library tab and click Scan in the toolbar. BMM walks your Mods Folder, discovers every subfolder, and populates the list. Each entry shows name, size, file count, and activation status.
tut.basics.scan.s2.title: Run a Scan
tut.basics.scan.s3.text: Click + Add mod in the toolbar to pick a folder or a .zip archive. BMM copies the content into your Mods Folder and registers it immediately — no scan needed. Use this for one-off additions.
tut.basics.scan.s3.title: Adding Mods Manually
tut.basics.scan.title: Scanning Mods
tut.basics.shared.s1.text: Sharing a single Mods Folder between two profiles is strongly discouraged. You risk activating a mod intended for another game, which can corrupt your installation. BMM will warn you if you try to share a folder.
tut.basics.shared.s1.title: ⚠️ Warning: Shared Mod Folders
tut.basics.shared.s2.text: If two game versions use identical file structures (e.g. an expansion and its base game), sharing is possible. Keep the game paths different and always verify the active profile before enabling mods.
tut.basics.shared.s2.title: When Sharing Can Be Safe
tut.basics.shared.title: Shared Folders (Optional)
tut.other.benchmark.s1.text: Mod activation involves copying potentially large files. Knowing your disk's real-world speed lets BMM set sensible I/O limits so activation does not degrade your system performance.
tut.other.benchmark.s1.title: Why Benchmark?
tut.other.benchmark.s2.text: Go to Settings & Other in the sidebar. Find the Performance & Benchmark section and click Open Benchmark. The dashboard shows live CPU, RAM, and Disk I/O graphs — use them to assess mod activation impact and fine-tune the I/O Limiter.
tut.other.benchmark.s2.title: Opening the Benchmark
tut.other.benchmark.title: Benchmark Dashboard
tut.other.bugreport.s1.text: If BMM crashes or behaves unexpectedly, use the built-in crash reporter. On the next launch, BMM detects the crash report, collects logs and system info, and offers to submit a report automatically.
tut.other.bugreport.s1.title: Found a Bug?
tut.other.bugreport.s2.text: BMM offers to send the crash report on startup. You can review its content before submitting. To file a manual report or a feature request, visit the GitHub Issues page linked in the Credits section.
tut.other.bugreport.s2.title: How to Report
tut.other.bugreport.title: Bug Reporting
tut.other.launchpack.s1.text: A BMM Launch Pack is a one-click shortcut that starts multiple applications or games at the same time. Great for launching your game alongside companion tools (overlay, capture software, voice chat) with a single icon.
tut.other.launchpack.s1.title: What is a BMM Launch Pack?
tut.other.launchpack.s2.text: Go to Settings & Other in the sidebar. Find the BMM Launch Pack section and click New Launch Pack. In the Create a Launch Pack dialog, name your pack, add the executables to launch, optionally set a custom icon, then confirm.
tut.other.launchpack.s2.title: Creating a Launch Pack
tut.other.launchpack.title: BMM Launchpack

tut.other.pluginsapi.title: Plugins & API
tut.other.pluginsapi.s1.title: What is the Plugin System?
tut.other.pluginsapi.s1.text: BMM supports community-made plugins that extend its functionality — custom actions, new UI panels, server integrations, and more. Head to the Plugins & API tab in the sidebar to get started.
tut.other.pluginsapi.s2.title: Installing a Plugin
tut.other.pluginsapi.s2.text: You can install plugins from the Catalog tab (click a card → Install) or import a .bmmplug file directly via the Import button. Once installed, the plugin appears in the Installed tab. This step is optional — skip it if the catalog is empty.
tut.other.pluginsapi.s2.action: Install or import a plugin to continue, or skip this step.
tut.other.pluginsapi.s3.title: Plugin Permissions
tut.other.pluginsapi.s3.text: Each plugin declares what it can access (file system, network, shell, etc.). The Permissions tab shows the current status per plugin. You can revoke a permission any time, or use the Global Trust toggle to allow all plugins at once — use with care.
tut.other.pluginsapi.s4.title: Script Generator
tut.other.pluginsapi.s4.text: The Script Generator lets you build automation scripts for your mod workflow without writing code. Pick an endpoint, add action blocks (copy, delete, run, move…), choose your output format (PowerShell, Python, Bash, Go…), and click Generate.
tut.other.pluginsapi.s5.title: BMM Local API
tut.other.pluginsapi.s5.text: BMM runs a local HTTP API on port 51274 (the default — it's configurable in Settings). The API tab lists every endpoint, its parameters, and lets you send live test requests directly from BMM. Third-party tools and plugins use this API to read mod lists, trigger activations, and sync with server repositories.
tut.other.pluginsapi.s6.title: API Token & Security
tut.other.pluginsapi.s6.text: All write endpoints require an API token. Go to the API tab → Settings, generate a token, and copy it. Tools that connect to BMM must include this token in the Authorization header. You can regenerate or revoke the token at any time.
tut.other.pluginsapi.s6.action: Copy your API token to continue.
tut.other.appcatalog.title: App Catalog
tut.other.appcatalog.s1.title: The App Catalog
tut.other.appcatalog.s1.text: The App Catalog (sidebar, highlighted) lets you discover, install, launch and update companion apps & tools — straight from BMM, in one click.
tut.other.appcatalog.s2.title: Finding apps
tut.other.appcatalog.s2.text: Use the search box and the category / price filters to narrow the list. Tabs above switch between Browse, Installed, Favorites and History.
tut.other.appcatalog.s3.title: Install, launch & update
tut.other.appcatalog.s3.text: Each card has an action: Install downloads (and verifies, when a checksum is provided) the app and tracks its version; installed cards switch to Launch, and offer an Update when a newer version ships. Only install from sources you trust.
tut.other.appcatalog.s4.title: Sources
tut.other.appcatalog.s4.text: The Sources tab manages where apps come from: official, partner and your own community catalog URLs. Add a URL to pull in more apps — remove any that fail to load.
tut.other.translate.title: Translation Tool
tut.other.translate.s1.title: Translate BMM yourself
tut.other.translate.s1.text: BMM ships a built-in Translation Sandbox so anyone can create or fix a language without touching code. It lives in Settings.
tut.other.translate.s2.title: Open the sandbox
tut.other.translate.s2.text: Click Translation Sandbox (highlighted). Edit translation keys in a safe sandbox — nothing changes in BMM until you export. You can even use pointer mode to click an element and jump straight to its key.
tut.other.translate.s3.title: Export & share
tut.other.translate.s3.text: When you're happy, export your language file and share it. Others import it via bmm://language/import or the language menu — and your translation becomes selectable app-wide.
tut.other.translate.s4.title: Thank you! 💛
tut.other.translate.s4.text: Community translations keep BMM accessible to everyone. Even fixing a few awkward strings helps a lot.
tut.other.themes.title: Theme System
tut.other.themes.s1.title: Make BMM yours
tut.other.themes.s1.text: The Theme System lets you restyle 100% of BMM — colours, fonts, shapes, even images and icons — with no CSS knowledge required. Power users still get raw CSS.
tut.other.themes.s2.title: Open the Theme Editor
tut.other.themes.s2.text: Click Open Theme Editor (highlighted). Start from one of the 7 presets, or pick a single colour and let the auto-palette generate a full coherent dark or light theme.
tut.other.themes.s3.title: Edit any element
tut.other.themes.s3.text: Use the eyedropper, then right-click any element to change its colours, hover state, CSS, icon or image. The Your changes panel tracks every edit with per-item revert — and Discard restores everything instantly.
tut.other.themes.s4.title: Save, share & install
tut.other.themes.s4.text: Save your theme, export it as a .bmmtheme file or copy a one-click share link, and browse the Theme Catalog for community themes.

docs.enableDisableDesc:
Unlike classic mod managers that create risky or unstable virtual links (symlinks), Better Mod Manager performs a smart physical copy of your files.

1. Activation: When you enable a mod, BMM analyzes the files. If they replace original game files, it discreetly copies them to your Backup folder. Then, it injects the mod files into the game.

2. Deactivation: When you disable the mod, BMM removes the mod files from the game, then instantly restores the original files from the Backup folder. Your game returns to its pure state.

Warning: Always make sure to disable a mod from the application before physically deleting its folder, otherwise the game will keep its modification files and the backup will not be restored.

docs.ioLimiterDesc:
The I/O Limiter prevents BMM from overwhelming your disks during mod operations.

Why? When you enable or disable large mods (several GBs), massive file copying can slow down your entire system — games, browser, streams.

How does it work? BMM splits each copy operation into small chunks and inserts micro-pauses between them to never exceed the speed limit you've set (in MB/s). Set 0 for unlimited speed.

Built-in Benchmark — Use the 'Benchmark Speed' button in the Storage Manager to automatically measure your disk speeds. BMM will then suggest an optimal value (70% of actual speed).

Cloud / NAS Storage — BMM automatically detects cloud drives (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox) and network storage (NAS). It is strongly recommended to limit speed on these drives as they are generally slower.

faq.a1: Yes! Each profile keeps its own mod state. When you return to a profile, your enabled mods are still there, even after a restart.
faq.a2: Technically none! .MM is simply a .JSON file renamed to make sharing between players easier.
faq.a3: You must first disable the mod so its files are removed from the game, then you can safely delete it.
faq.a4: Disable the mod, replace its files in the mods folder, then re-enable it. The backup will be recreated automatically.
faq.a5: BMM uses a stacked system. The last mod you enable has priority. But don't worry: if you disable it, BMM will automatically restore the previous mod's file or the original!
faq.a6: Yes! Use the Archive Explorer in the mod details to navigate folders and even open files directly.
faq.a7: It's often because the mod is very large (many files or several GBs). If the mods folder and the game are not on the same hard drive, copying may be slowed down by your drive speeds.
faq.a8: BMM checks the space before each copy. If the disk is full, activation is blocked for safety, even if alerts are disabled in the settings.
faq.a9: No. Unlike visual alerts, blocking in case of a saturated disk is vital to prevent data or system corruption.
faq.aBenchValues: The performance graph monitors the entire disk, not just BMM. If you limit BMM to 10 MB/s, but Windows, your browser, or your antivirus use 2 MB/s in the background, the graph will show 12 MB/s. BMM always strictly respects its own internal limit.
faq.aCrash: BMM uses a 'clean shutdown flag'. On each startup, it checks if the previous session ended normally. If not, a report is automatically generated.
faq.aCreatorId: The Creator ID is a unique hardware fingerprint generated by BMM from your machine. It identifies your client to the server without requiring a login — the server admin can use it to whitelist or ban users persistently, even if their IP address changes.
faq.aDiscord: Go to settings and toggle 'Enable Discord RPC'. If Discord is running, BMM will automatically update your status. Ensure that 'Activity Status' is public in your Discord user settings.
faq.aHidden: Not really 'hidden', but less known: auto-calibration adjusts your speed limits based on real disk load at startup.
faq.aHostOwn: Yes! BMM is designed for self-hosting. You can use any Linux VPS (Ubuntu recommended). Refer to the dedicated deployment guide in the 'Advanced' tab.
faq.aIntegrity: BMM calculates a unique cryptographic hash for every file. This ensures that mods haven't been corrupted or tampered with. The system can detect even single-bit changes, guaranteeing that what you download is exactly what the mod author intended.
faq.aIo: It prevents BMM from copying files too fast, which could lag your PC. Go to Settings → Storage Manager to adjust the speed limit per disk.
faq.aJsTs: BMM v0.9+ has migrated to TypeScript (TS) for better stability. However, the Modern ESM system requires that imports use the .js extension because they reference the final files that stay in the browser/Tauri after compilation.
faq.aLimit: BMM now includes safety features. If your free space drops below the warning threshold, you'll get a warning. If it drops below the critical threshold, installation will be blocked to protect your system.
faq.aLuxStd: The Lux version includes a web-based monitoring dashboard for your repository, ideal for visualizing server status. The STD version is ultra-lightweight, with no UI, perfect for VPS with very low RAM.
faq.aModpacks: BMM Modpacks use SHA-256 fingerprints to uniquely identify mod files. This ensures every player uses exactly the same version, regardless of where mods are stored. If mods are missing, BMM can download them automatically from the ServerRepo (if available). If a file was merely moved by mistake, BMM will find and restore it locally without downloading anything.
faq.aOneClick: Only direct download links (DDL) are compatible. A DDL starts the download immediately without going through an intermediate page. GitHub 'Releases' links or direct links to a file on a private server are perfect.
faq.aPat_intro: A Personal Access Token (PAT) lets you download more than 60 mods/hour from GitHub. Here's how to create one:
faq.aPat_s1: Log in to github.com with your account.
faq.aPat_s3: Scroll down in the left menu to Developer settings (very bottom).
faq.aPat_s6: Give it a name (e.g. BMM Downloads), choose an expiry, and check only public_repo under repo.
faq.aPat_s7: Click Generate token, copy it (it starts with ghp_) and paste it into the GitHub PAT field in BMM Settings.
faq.aPat_warn: Never share your token! It grants access to your GitHub account.
faq.aRepo: The Server Repo is a feature that allows you to host your own mod repository or connect to someone else's. It synchronizes mods between users via HTTP, ensuring everyone has the same version and configuration.
faq.aRepoHosting: Yes! BMM supports both approaches. You can host directly from your PC for local sharing (LAN) or use a VPS/dedicated server for 24/7 availability. The application generates all assets required for hosting on any standard web server.
faq.aRepoPublic: You need to forward port 8000 (TCP) on your router, or use the UPnP feature available in the Server Repo tab.
faq.aResumable: BMM splits large files into 4MB chunks. If an error occurs (internet disconnection, crash, or closure), BMM checks which chunks are already validated and only downloads the missing parts.
faq.aSemantic: Classic mode uses standard string matching. Semantic mode is much more advanced: it normalizes your query (removes accents/case), splits it into keywords, and performs a weighted intersection. This allows it to index not only titles but also the full Tasky descriptions and hidden metadata inside interactive diagrams, showing a match percentage for partial results.
faq.aServerSeed: The Server Seed is a secret string that defines your server's persistent identity. Ban lists and whitelist rules are tied to it — so restarting or redeploying the server keeps all your admin settings intact. Leave the field empty when exporting to auto-generate one, or paste a previous seed to reuse an existing identity.
faq.aThreads: No. BMM uses a high-performance multi-threaded engine in Rust. Heavy tasks like file copying or hash calculation run in dedicated background threads, keeping the main UI thread (and your PC) fast and responsive.
faq.aTokio: Tokio is Rust's asynchronous runtime. BMM uses it to handle thousands of concurrent I/O operations efficiently, ensuring that file transfers, network requests, and background tasks never block the UI.
faq.aZipTime: BMM performs two intensive tasks: first, it calculates a unique digital fingerprint (SHA-256) for every file to guarantee perfect synchronization. Second, it compresses everything into a single archive. For 20GB+, this is a massive I/O and CPU operation.
faq.betahub.a1: Reports include the title, description, and steps you provided. If enabled, system logs and DxDiag are attached privately; they are strictly reserved for the dev team and never shared publicly.
faq.betahub.a2: This is the Proof-of-Work (PoW) security check. It's a cryptographic calculation that verifies you're a human and prevents spam bots without requiring intrusive image captchas.
faq.betahub.a3: The development team will reach out to you directly via the contact information you provided (Discord or Email) if more details are needed or if an update is available.

faq.aDocker: Docker is a containerization system: it bundles the BMM server and all its dependencies into an isolated box. Result — one command to start the server, regardless of the OS (Windows, Linux, macOS), with nothing to install manually.
faq.aNgrok: ngrok creates an encrypted tunnel between your local machine and the Internet. Without opening ports on your router, clients access your server via a public HTTPS URL (e.g. https://abc123.ngrok-free.app). Ideal for home hosting.

docs.modStructure.title: How BMM works
docs.modStructure.paths3intro: Every profile in BMM relies on 3 paths you configure once:
docs.modStructure.pathGameDesc: Where the game is installed. BMM copies active mod files here.
docs.modStructure.pathModsDesc: The folder where you store all your mods. BMM scans it to build your list.
docs.modStructure.pathBackupDesc: BMM saves the original game files here before replacing them.
docs.modStructure.activateTitle: What happens when you activate a mod
docs.modStructure.activateSteps:
• BMM scans the mod folder and lists all its files.
  • For each file, if a game original exists at the same path and hasn't been backed up yet, BMM copies it to the backup folder.
  • BMM then copies the mod file into the game folder, at the exact matching path.
  • The mod is active — the game sees the mod files in their normal location.
docs.modStructure.deactivateTitle: What happens when you deactivate a mod
docs.modStructure.deactivateSteps:
• BMM removes the files it copied into the game folder.
  • If a backup existed, it is restored — the game gets its original files back.
  • If multiple mods were active on the same file (stacking), BMM restores the previous mod's file.
docs.modStructure.ruleDesc: Each mod file must have the same relative sub-path as its target in the game. BMM uses this to know exactly where to copy. The mod only needs to contain the files it changes.
docs.modStructure.exampleBadge: Generic example — actual paths depend on your game
docs.modStructure.treeNote2: This mod only touches the textures.
docs.modStructure.ruleFooter: BMM takes Data/Skins/hero_skin.png from the mod and copies it to the same path in game_path. Files not in the mod (game.exe, Config/…) are never touched.
docs.modStructure.practical: In practice: most mods are already distributed in the correct format. Place the mod folder in your BMM mods folder and BMM will detect it automatically. Never manually delete files from the game folder without going through BMM — always use the Activate / Deactivate buttons.
docs.symlinks.title: How symbolic links work
docs.symlinks.desc: When you enable a mod in BMM, here is what actually happens:
docs.symlinks.step1: BMM scans the mod folder and reconstructs the folder tree
docs.symlinks.step2: For each file/folder, BMM creates a symbolic link in the game folder pointing to your mod
docs.symlinks.step3: The game sees the files as if they were really in its folder — without copying
docs.symlinks.step4: Disabling the mod just removes the symbolic links — your original files are intact
docs.symlinks.warn: Symbolic links require administrator rights on Windows (or developer mode enabled). BMM will ask to elevate permissions if needed. Never manually delete files in the game folder if they are BMM links — always use the "Disable" button in BMM.
tut.basics.moddetails.title: Reading a Mod's Details
tut.basics.moddetails.s1.title: Open the Detail Panel
tut.basics.moddetails.s1.text:
Click any mod card in the Library to open its detail panel on the right. This panel is your single source of truth for everything BMM knows about that mod — no need to dig through folders.
💡

Click another card to switch the panel — it always reflects the currently selected mod.
tut.basics.moddetails.s2.title: What the Panel Shows
tut.basics.moddetails.s2.text:
The detail panel breaks a mod down into:
  • Name, version & author — editable metadata (the pencil icon lets you correct it).
  • Size & file count — how much disk space it uses and how many files it ships.
  • File tree — the exact folders/files inside the mod, so you can check its structure before mapping.
  • Dependencies — other mods this one needs (BMM warns you if any are missing).
  • Activation order — the # number shown once the mod is active.
tut.basics.moddetails.s3.title: Per-Mod Actions
tut.basics.moddetails.s3.text:
From the detail panel you can also rename the mod, open its folder on disk, verify its integrity, or delete it. Reorder its activation priority by dragging it within the active-mods list.
💡

The detail panel is the fastest way to debug a mod that "isn't working" — check its file tree and dependencies first.
tut.basics.integrity.s3.title: Fixing a Failed Check
tut.basics.integrity.s3.text:
A failed check usually means a game update overwrote a mod file, or a download was incomplete. To fix it:
  • Re-activate the mod (toggle Off then On) — BMM re-copies its files from the Mods Folder.
  • If the source is also damaged, re-add the mod from a fresh archive.
⚠️
